answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because timber only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any onyx approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
